title: Library System
story: A small community library needs a simple system to track books. When someone borrows a book, it's marked checked out. When they return it, it's available again. You can build this with one struct and two methods.
why: Methods that mutate struct fields let you model real-world state changes like checking out a book.
analogy: A library book is like a light switch — it can be either ON (checked out) or OFF (available). The `checkout` and `return_book` methods flip the switch.
try_it: Add a `due_date: Str` field to Book (e.g., "2026-08-01"). Modify `checkout` to set the due date to 14 days from now. Add a method `is_overdue` that always returns false for now.
tips: Methods that mutate use `self` without `&mut` — the compiler handles the borrowing
Inside a method, field access is direct: write `checked_out`, not `self.checked_out`
A method that only reads fields still uses `self` as the first parameter
common_mistakes: Writing `self.checked_out` inside the method — XIOM fields are accessed directly without `self.`
Forgetting the `self` parameter in the method signature entirely
